4._section_summary: This Results section describes an exploratory factor analysis of the 15-item CEMS (Childhood Eating Messages Scale) conducted on 238 participants. Using parallel analysis, two factors were retained: Pressure to Eat Messages (PEM) with 5 items accounting for 33.69% of variance, and Restrictive and Critical Messages (RCM) with 5 items accounting for 26.64% of variance. The final 10-item CEMS was used in subsequent analyses.

5._section_summary: This section reports reliability and validity analyses for the CEMS (Caregiver Eating Messages Scale) and presents structural equation modeling results examining relationships among caregiver eating messages, body acceptance, body appreciation, and intuitive eating. The study includes a main sample of 238 participants (160 women, 78 men) and a test-retest subsample of 18 young adult students (56% women, 44% men, M age = 20.65, 94% Caucasian).
